correctness.rationale: For integer d>=3 and independently surface-uniform endpoints conditioned on opposite last-coordinate signs (probability 1/2), the exact linear crossing is Z=[B sqrt(1-A^2)u+A sqrt(1-B^2)v]/(A+B). Standard Gaussian sphere normalization gives (sqrt(d)A,sqrt(d)B) => independent half normals; independent equatorial directions satisfy E[(u·v)^2]=1/(d-1), so the cross term vanishes. Therefore Q_d => (X²+Y²)/(X+Y)². The ratio X/Y is half-Cauchy; W=|X-Y|/(X+Y) has density 4/[pi(1+w²)] on (0,1). The transformation Q=(1+W²)/2 yields precisely the displayed CDF 4/pi atan(sqrt(2q-1)) and density 2/[pi q sqrt(2q-1)], with means 2/pi and 4/(3pi), variance strictly positive. Q_d is bounded in [0,1] so all positive bounded moments converge; rotational invariance yields independent uniform angular component in each finite d. A weak law on changing dimensions is not a common-space direction limit. No quantitative rate proved.
